topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture topic, learning outcomes, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Proliferative Signaling and Growth Inhibition Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in signaling cascades such as Wnt/beta-catenin, RTK-MAPK, and PI3K-AKT drive sustained proliferation and evade growth suppression.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Tumor Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how blocks in terminal cell differentiation contribute to malignancy in both hematological and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how mutations in p53 and apoptotic regulatory proteins enable cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit via telomerase activation alongside the normal p53-mediated stress and senescence response.

topics.label: Metabolic Rewiring and the Warburg Effect
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics transition to complex cancer hallmarks and examine the mechanisms of altered cellular metabolism, including aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolite signaling.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the biological necessity, timing, and regulatory balance of new blood vessel formation in supporting tumor growth.

topics.label: Metastasis and Circulatory Dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the multistep cascade of metastatic spread, its anatomical routes, diagnostic tracking, and associated genomic alterations.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks conclude the lecture by summarising the integration of cancer hallmarks, referencing recent literature, and inviting questions.
